questions.text: The README lists a `:reset_ids` option for the deletion strategy — what does it actually do, and does every adapter support it?
questions.how_found: Read database_cleaner-active_record/README.md (line 64 documents :reset_ids), then opened lib/database_cleaner/active_record/deletion.rb. `delete_tables` calls `reset_id_sequence` per table when @reset_ids is set; `reset_id_sequence` (29-40) switches on connection.adapter_name: Mysql2/Trilogy -> ALTER TABLE ... AUTO_INCREMENT = 1, SQLite -> delete from sqlite_sequence, PostgreSQL -> reset_pk_sequence!, anything else raises "reset_id option not supported for ...". So no, not every adapter.
questions.why_asked: It is one of the few options in the README whose behaviour is database-specific, and a newcomer turning it on needs to know whether it will blow up on their engine.

questions.text: What values does the `:truncate_option` option accept, what is the default, and where does it end up in the generated SQL?
questions.how_found: Grepped the workspace for truncate_option. Truncation#initialize (8-9) rejects any key outside [:only, :except, :pre_count, :cache_tables, :reset_ids, :truncate_option] with an ArgumentError, and line 17 defaults it to :restrict. It is passed through #clean (24, 26) and only PostgreSQLAdapter#truncate_tables (202) interpolates it: "TRUNCATE TABLE ... RESTART IDENTITY #{opts[:truncate_option]};" — so :cascade/:restrict, Postgres only.
questions.why_asked: Newcomers hit Postgres foreign-key errors on truncation and want to know whether CASCADE is available and how to ask for it.

questions.text: Our suite dies with "As you have more than one active sequel database you have to specify the one to use manually!" — where does that come from and what do I set?
questions.how_found: Grepped for the message text. DatabaseCleaner::Sequel::Base#db returns @db only when it was explicitly set to something other than :default; otherwise it raises if ::Sequel::DATABASES.count > 1, and falls back to ::Sequel::DATABASES.first. The fix is documented in the sequel README (lines 65-75): DatabaseCleaner[:sequel].db = Sequel.connect(uri), or DatabaseCleaner[:sequel, db: ...].
questions.rg_query: rg -n 'more than one active sequel database'
questions.why_asked: It is the first hard failure anyone opening a second Sequel connection in tests will see, and the message does not say which setter to use.

questions.text: What does `DatabaseCleaner.clean_with(:truncation)` do differently from setting `strategy = :truncation` and then calling `clean`?
questions.how_found: Grepped clean_with: core.rb:14 delegates it to Cleaners, cleaners.rb:57-60 runs the Safeguard then fans out to every cleaner, and Cleaner#clean_with (62-67) builds a throwaway strategy object, points it at the current db and cleans once — it never assigns @strategy, so the configured strategy is left untouched. That is why the README's RSpec example can clean_with(:truncation) in before(:suite) while keeping :transaction per example.
questions.why_asked: Both calls appear in the README's copy-paste RSpec config and it is not obvious that one of them is a one-shot that does not change global state.

questions.text: Why does my suite abort immediately when the connection string points at a shared staging machine instead of my laptop?
questions.how_found: Read database_cleaner/lib/database_cleaner/cleaners.rb, where start/clean/cleaning/clean_with all begin with Safeguard.new.run; Safeguard::CHECKS runs RemoteDatabaseUrl first. It URI-parses ENV['DATABASE_URL'], returns false for sqlite/sqlite3 schemes, for a blank host, for localhost/127.0.0.1 (the LOCAL constant) and for any host ending in '.local'; anything else is treated as off-box and raises. It is skipped via the DATABASE_CLEANER_ALLOW_REMOTE_DATABASE_URL env var, DatabaseCleaner.allow_remote_database_url, or by setting a url_allowlist.
questions.why_asked: A newcomer whose team shares a dev database sees the run die before a single example executes and needs to know what refused, and how to opt out for legitimate cases.

questions.text: Is there a way to disable wiping entirely for a suite, without ripping the setup out of my helper?
questions.how_found: Traced Cleaner#strategy in database_cleaner/lib/database_cleaner/cleaner.rb:55-57: it memoizes NullStrategy.new whenever nothing was assigned, and strategy= with nil leaves @strategy nil, so it falls back here. NullStrategy implements the whole interface as no-ops — start, db=, clean do nothing and cleaning simply yields the block through. The core README calls it the `null` strategy and says you can select it explicitly with `nil`.
questions.why_asked: When someone is debugging a leaky test they want to turn the whole mechanism off for one run and see what breaks, without deleting the hooks.

questions.text: For Rails, how does the default mode undo everything a test wrote without ever issuing a removal statement?
questions.how_found: database_cleaner-active_record/lib/database_cleaner/active_record.rb:10 sets the default to :transaction. Transaction#start leases/checks out a connection (lease_connection on ActiveRecord >= 7.2, connection below that), runs an empty `connection.transaction {}` as a warm-up hack, then opens a non-joinable transaction. #clean walks every connection in the pool, takes its lock, and rolls back any connection with open_transactions > 0, then releases the connection back to the pool. Nothing is ever physically removed.
questions.why_asked: It is the default everyone inherits; understanding that it depends on a single pooled connection explains the classic Capybara 'my record is missing' failure described in the core README.

questions.text: Vendors need their own wiping commands — is there a single spot that chooses the vendor-specific code and mixes it in at runtime?
questions.how_found: Truncation#clean (21-31) works against `connection`, which is a ConnectionWrapper (a SimpleDelegator). Its constructor is the only dispatch point: it always extends AbstractAdapter, then switches on connection.adapter_name — Mysql2/Trilogy get AbstractMysqlAdapter; SQLite gets AbstractMysqlAdapter plus SQLiteAdapter; PostgreSQL/PostGIS get AbstractMysqlAdapter plus PostgreSQLAdapter. The modules that follow (86-254) override truncate_tables, pre_count_tables, database_tables and the table cache. ConnectionWrapper is declared private_constant at line 256.
questions.why_asked: Before adding support for another engine (or debugging odd SQL), you need to know whether dispatch is centralised or sprinkled through conditionals.

questions.text: Is there logic that skips the wipe entirely when nothing has changed since the previous cycle?
questions.how_found: Sequel Truncation#start (12-14) records `txid`, and #clean (16-17) returns straight away unless `dirty?`. `dirty?` compares the stored value with a fresh one; `txid` only returns a value on Postgres (SELECT txid_snapshot_xmax(txid_current_snapshot())) and is nil everywhere else, so on other engines `@last_txid.nil?` keeps it always dirty. Deletion inherits the same guard (deletion.rb:36).
questions.why_asked: Suite speed is the reason people pick a strategy, so you want to know whether a no-op example still pays for a round trip — and the answer turns out to be engine-dependent.

questions.text: How do we keep the server from rejecting removals because of parent/child links, and is the previous state put back afterwards?
questions.how_found: Sequel Deletion#clean (35-44) wraps everything in db.transaction and hands the work to disable_referential_integrity. On Postgres it issues SET CONSTRAINTS ALL DEFERRED and DISABLE TRIGGER ALL per table; on MySQL it reads @@FOREIGN_KEY_CHECKS into a local, sets it to 0, and the ensure block re-enables triggers / restores the saved value. Note the MySQL restore reads `old`, a local variable of the enclosing method — and the ensure branch also runs on engines where nothing was disabled.
questions.why_asked: Anyone whose schema has foreign keys wants to know whether cleanup can corrupt or leave enforcement switched off if an example blows up mid-run.

questions.text: Our Sequel test run refuses to start with "ENV['RAILS_ENV'] is set to production" — I grepped the sequel adapter and found nothing. Where is that check?
questions.how_found: database_cleaner-sequel/lib/database_cleaner/sequel.rb only requires database_cleaner/core and registers strategies; the guard lives in the core gem. Cleaners#start/#clean/#cleaning/#clean_with (database_cleaner/lib/database_cleaner/cleaners.rb:40-60) each call Safeguard.new.run, and Safeguard::Production scans KEYS = ENV, APP_ENV, RACK_ENV, RAILS_ENV for the value 'production'. Escape hatches: the DATABASE_CLEANER_ALLOW_PRODUCTION env var or DatabaseCleaner.allow_production (core.rb:18).
questions.why_asked: The failure surfaces while running the Sequel suite, so the obvious place to look is the Sequel gem — but adapters contain no safety logic at all, which is worth learning on day one.

questions.text: The adapter specs start with `it_should_behave_like "a database_cleaner adapter"` — where is that shared example defined and what does it actually assert?
questions.how_found: database_cleaner-sequel/spec/database_cleaner/sequel_spec.rb:5 and database_cleaner-active_record/spec/database_cleaner/active_record_spec.rb:5 use it after `require 'database_cleaner/spec'`, which is shipped by the core gem (database_cleaner/lib/database_cleaner/spec.rb). The adapter example enumerates DatabaseCleaner::Cleaner.available_strategies(described_class), instantiates each constant and reuses the 'a database_cleaner strategy' example (3-9), which only asserts the object responds to db, db=, start, clean and cleaning. ADAPTERS.md:103 spells out that it checks method existence only, not that cleaning works.
questions.why_asked: It is the first line of both adapter test suites and there is no definition in either repo; a newcomer writing a new adapter needs to know what contract it really enforces.
